title: Secret Service guarded the dying von Neumann at a naval hospital
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Secret Service guarded the dying von Neumann at a naval hospital, about 1957 at naval hospital (Walter Reed / Bethesda), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: he had uh cir secret service outside of uh the naval hospital that he that he was in because they were afraid of what he might say.
He died and there were secret service outside of his [music] hospital room because they were worried that he was going to talk.
tellings.difference: Told by Deep Prasad, who does not name the naval hospital.
tellings.link_reason: The same claim that the Secret Service guarded the dying von Neumann's hospital room in 1957 for fear of what he would say.

as_told.title: Secret Service guarding von Neumann's deathbed

tellings.quote: He also I believe he died in a Maryland hospital that I think it was a Navy hospital and there were I think secret service outside of the his hospital room because they were worried that he was going to talk.
tellings.difference: Places the hospital in Maryland and is hedged ('I believe', 'I think').
tellings.link_reason: Same account: Secret Service guarding the dying von Neumann at a Navy hospital in case he talked.

as_told.title: Von Neumann guarded on his deathbed in a Navy hospital

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that when the famous mathematician John von Neumann lay dying in a naval hospital in 1957, the Secret Service was posted outside his room because they were afraid of what he might say. The suggestion is that he knew secrets the government badly wanted kept.
